Authors: Thiago Altair, Emma Lindenfelser, Douglas Galante, Hamilton Varela, Yannick De Decker, Reuben Hudson

Redox gradients across vent minerals driving electron flow have long been proposed as a prebiotic means for chemical reductions.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cc04072a

item.title: Recent advances in fluorescence analysis of chemical warfare agents using organic probes
item.description:
Authors: Xinxin Li, Fengniu Lu, Baili Zhao, Zhiqin Yuan, Kai Zhang, Chao Lu

A summary of recent progress in organic probe-mediated detection of nerve agents and blister agents has been provided based on the reaction mechanism.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cc05673c

item.title: A high-capacity N-heterocyclic porous polymer for sustainable all-polymer seawater batteries at subzero temperatures
item.description:
Authors: Yuanzhe Lu, Xiu Liu, Zhongheng Sun, Zishou Zhang, Bang Lan, Linfeng Zhong, Dingshan Yu

A microporous N-heterocyclic polymer enables high-capacity and high-rate charge storage in natural seawater, affording an all-polymer seawater battery with high output voltage, high energy efficiency, and direct seawater activation at −4 °C.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cc06025k

item.title: Supramolecular networks with built-in Li + transport pathways for SiO x anodes in lithium-ion batteries
item.description:
Authors: Feng Zhou, Chuxiong Huang, Yeshuang Song, Shuxing Wu, Xiujuan Wei, Zhan Lin

Supramolecular crosslinked LFGA binders with built-in Li + transport channels were constructed to address the volumetric expansion and sluggish ion kinetics of SiO x anodes in lithium-ion batteries.

DOI: 10.1039/d6cc05807h

item.title: Terminal 4-Cyanophenyl Functionalization of Helical Nanographenes: Mechanistic Insights into Columnar Assembly and Near-Infrared Chiroptical Modulation
item.description:
Authors: ZHIBO LIU, Takashi Hirose

We report a primary helical nanographene terminally functionalized with 4-cyanophenyl groups. This terminal substitution dictates columnar solid-state assembly and selectively stabilizes frontier orbitals deriving narrow HOMO-LUMO gap. It also induces...

DOI: 10.1039/d6cc06209a

item.title: Solution-phase formation of proquinoidal conjugated polymer nanowires with rapid photothermal response
item.description:
Authors: Jian-De Dong, Jiao Wu, Si-Yu Ji, Tian-Xiong Wang, Shu-Yao Tian, Xu-Hui Jin

Solution-phase access to well-defined nanowires from a non-block proquinoidal polymer enables rapid photothermal heating and low-loading solar water evaporation.
